# Kentucky, United States Genealogy

Kentucky became the 15th state admitted to the Union on June 1, 1792. Originally part of [Virginia](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Virginia,_United_States_Genealogy), it was organized from three initial counties: Fayette, Jefferson, and Lincoln. The state currently includes 120 counties, with Frankfort as its capital.

## Historical Settlement

In 1775, Daniel Boone ushered the first settlers into Kentucky along the Wilderness Road, through the Cumberland Gap. Significant migration occurred around statehood and continued into the early 1800s.

## Record Types Available

Genealogy records are kept on the county level in the United States, making identification of the correct county essential.

### Vital Records
Civil registration of births, marriages, and deaths. County-level marriage records date from county formation. Statewide birth and death registration began in 1911 with general compliance by 1917. See [Kentucky Vital Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Kentucky_Vital_Records).

### Census Records
Federal census enumerations from 1810 for most Kentucky counties. State censuses were not taken.

### Court Records
County courthouses hold probate records, guardianship files, civil and criminal cases, and naturalization records.

### Land and Property Records
Kentucky is a state-land state. Land grants were issued by both Virginia (before 1792) and Kentucky (after 1792). County deeds record person-to-person transfers. See [Kentucky Land and Property](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Kentucky_Land_and_Property).

### Church Records
Before 1900 the largest religious groups in Kentucky were the Baptist, Methodist, Roman Catholic, and Presbyterian churches. See [Kentucky Church Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Kentucky_Church_Records).

### Military Records
Service records, pension files, and bounty land warrants at the National Archives. Kentucky state adjutant general records at KDLA.

## Key Repositories

- **Kentucky Department for Libraries and Archives (KDLA)** — Frankfort; holds state-level records and microfilmed county records
- **Kentucky Historical Society** — Frankfort; holds manuscripts, newspapers, and genealogical collections
- **County courthouses** — primary holders of county-level records
- **University of Kentucky Special Collections** — Lexington
